key_insight: In MAPbI3 precursor inks, Ti3C2Tx MXenes are destabilized by I2/polyiodides and, more slowly, by PbI2, while MAI can passivate and stabilize the MXene surface through hydrogen bonding.
engineering_relevance: The order and composition of perovskite precursor addition can directly control MXene survival and surface chemistry, making ink formulation a key design lever for reliable MXene–perovskite optoelectronic devices.
method: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) to track MXene surface composition and oxidation state changes
Density functional theory (DFT) to explain adsorption and reaction mechanisms of precursor species
Comparative exposure tests with individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a combined experimental-theoretical study that links observed MXene degradation/stabilization trends to specific precursor species and their interaction mechanisms.
watch_item: MXene stability is sequence-dependent, so changing precursor mixing order can unintentionally alter surface chemistry and degradation behavior during ink processing.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
